doctrine: Sequence load-reduction measures (envelope, controls/RCx) before plant replacement decisions wherever the capital timeline allows — replacing equipment against an unreduced load leads to oversizing

Anchor every measure to a capital event: re-roof, refinance/capital-raise, unit turn, or forced equipment end-of-life. Standalone measures with no anchoring event are the hardest to get funded and the first to slip
Never force replacement of equipment with meaningful remaining useful life unless a compliance deadline or repeated-failure signal makes deferral riskier than acting now

Coordinate tenant-disruption classes across measures in the same stage: batch in-unit and vacancy-required work together at unit turnover rather than re-entering occupied units repeatedly for separate projects

The staging plan is a sequence with dependencies, not a flat list — state explicitly what must happen before what (e.g. envelope air-sealing before HVAC right-sizing; panel capacity study before any electrification stage)
Revisit the staging plan at each capital event; a plan built once at underwriting goes stale as equipment ages and rates/incentives change
origination_prompts: What capital events are already on ownership's calendar in the next 1-5 years (re-roof, refinance, planned unit renovations)? Attach retrofit measures to these first.
Which pieces of equipment are within 2 years of PCA-estimated end-of-life? These anchor the near-term stages.
Are there measures that only make sense if sequenced after another (load reduction before right-sizing, panel study before electrification)? Map the dependency chain explicitly.
Where do tenant-disruption classes cluster? Can in-unit or vacancy-required measures be batched into existing unit-turn schedules?
feasibility_checks: Confirm the assumed capital events (re-roof, refinance) are actually budgeted and scheduled by ownership, not just plausible
Verify no stage assumes financing or incentive availability (rebates, green loans) that hasn't been confirmed for this property and timeline
Check that dependency ordering is enforceable — e.g. that the load-reduction stage will actually complete before the plant-replacement decision point in the schedule
Name each stage's tenant-disruption class explicitly (none/light/in-unit/vacancy-required) and confirm property management has agreed to the disruption schedule
data_requirements: walk-the-pca output (system inventory, condition, immediate repairs, deferred capex)
